query: For a high-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution and exhibiting a favorable strength–ductility combination, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading? Explain the hypothesized mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the same alloy tested under identical conditions without the intervention, define the applicable exposure and loading regime, identify supporting evidence from prior observations, and specify an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.target_system: High-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution

generation.hypothesis: The high-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution will preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading if the solid solution strengthening mechanism is maintained.
generation.intervention: Control of impurities and optimization of composition
generation.conditions: Thermal exposure at 700°C and subsequent loading
generation.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and dislocation-mediated plasticity, derived from materials-science principles and supported by records node::10.1002/adma.201807142 and node::10.1016/j.scriptamat.2020.07.004
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 500-900°C and loading conditions
generation.uncertainty: Effects of impurities and composition optimization on solid solution strengthening

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructure analysis after thermal exposure and loading
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy without intervention shows similar or improved toughness and strength-ductility combination, the hypothesis is falsified.

Own digest: Origin of age softening in the refractory high-entropy alloys

Abstract: AbstractRefractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are emerging materials with potential for use under extreme conditions. As a newly developed material system, a comprehensive understanding of their long-term stability under potential service temperatures remains to be established. This study examined a titanium-vanadium-niobium-tantalum alloy, a promising RHEA known for its superior high-temperature strength and room-temperature ductility. Using a combination of advanced analytical microscopies, Calculation of Phase Diagrams (CALPHAD) software, and nanoindentation, we investigated the evolution of its microstructure and mechanical properties upon aging at 700°C. Trace interstitials such as oxygen and nitrogen, initially contributing to solid solution strengthening, promote phase segregation during thermal aging.
